title: problem
description: What went wrong, in the one shape every app uses (ADR-S21): an error, when the request failed, in an answer's errors; or a problem the answer worked around, in its problems. type, title and detail follow RFC 9457 Problem Details; reason, at, apiVersion and kind are this shape's extensions. A program decides by type and reason, never by title or detail (G-STACK-15). A field that does not apply is left out, never null.

apiVersion.description: Always elderlygate/contracts/problem/v1: names this schema wherever the Problem appears, so it can be read even on its own (ADR-S15).

kind.description: Always Problem, so a problem is told apart from every other kind, even outside an answer.

type.description: What happened, as an open word a program decides by; a plain word is a relative URI reference, as RFC 9457 allows. A reader matches the words it knows and shows the detail for any other, so an app can report a new word without a new contract (CT-RULE-1). Known words: unread: a part was left out and the rest kept; refused: the whole thing was not taken; undeclared: it names something that is not declared; old: it is in an old form, which a migrate fixes; unsupported_contract: the asked contract version is not served; the app's version answer lists the versions it serves (ADR-S03); not_found: the thing asked for is not there; failed: the app itself broke, not the request; the reason says whether something must be fixed before trying again.

title.description: A short text for the type, the same every time it happens, for people. A program reads type and reason instead, so this text may be reworded. Left out when the app has none.

detail.description: What went wrong in this occurrence, in plain words for a person. A program reads type and reason instead, never this text, so it may be reworded.

reason.description: Why it happened, when a program needs more than the type to decide; an open word, read like type. Left out when the type says enough. Known words: wrong_type: a value is of another type than the field takes; empty: a value that must say something is empty; unknown_key: a key the shape does not have; out_of_range: a value outside what the field allows; duplicate: another place already holds the same thing; token: the request came without the app's token, or with a wrong one; host: the request named a host the app does not answer on; origin: the request came from a page that is not the app's own; not_json: the request body is not JSON; unconfirmed: a change was sent without the user's yes, so nothing was changed; config_unreadable: the app could not read its own settings; core_needs_values: the app cannot start, as values it needs are not set; feature_needs_values: a feature is on but values it needs are not set; too_many_streams: the server already keeps the most event streams it takes; queue_timeout: the change waited longer than the queue allows for its turn and did not run; not_read_back: the change ran, but what it wrote could not be read back; ticket_lost: another process took the change's waiting ticket for stale, so the change did not run; queue_unusable: the change queue's folder cannot be made, read or written; queue_backend_unsupported: the change queue names a backend this build does not run, or its marker cannot be read; change_too_long: the app's own write held the queue's turn past its limit; too_large: the request body is larger than the app takes.

at.description: Where it happened: the first place is where it happened, any others what it clashes with, so a person or a tool goes straight to them. Left out when the problem is about no place.

place.description: One place a problem points to. Every field is optional, as a problem may know only the file, or only the field, but a place says at least one thing.

file.description: The file, as a path inside the folder the app works on, so the same problem reads the same on every machine; never a machine path, so it has no leading slash or backslash, no drive letter or scheme such as file:, no leading ~ or space, and no .. step.

document.description: Which document in that file or input, counted from 1, as one file may hold several.

line.description: The line where it starts in the real file, counted from 1, so an editor can jump there.

path.description: The field inside the document, as a path such as metadata.id, so a person finds the exact value to fix.
